sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a house in Wilmette?
sections.html:
Wilmette levies its own real estate transfer tax: $3 for every $1,000 of consideration, or fraction of $1,000, under an ordinance the Village Board adopted in 1988. The buyer is responsible for it, so it shows up on the buyer's side of the settlement statement. The state separately taxes the transfer at 50 cents per $500 of declared value under 35 ILCS 200/31-10.

The village will not release the stamps until the seller's utility account is clear, which ties buyer and seller together in the days before closing. Exempt transfers are filed under Chapter 9-15.6 of the village code, so a trust transfer or similar deed should be reviewed with Finance before the closing date.

sections.h2: How do the Wilmette final meter read and stamps work together?
sections.html:
The seller or a representative must ask Finance for a final meter reading about two weeks before the date it is needed, by phone at 847-853-7607 or through the online request. The village confirms the request within two business days, and the read itself happens three business days before closing. Stamps are released once the seller and buyer have paid all outstanding bills.

Wilmette sale timeline from the Village Finance Department pages
TimingWhoAction
Two weeks before the read dateSellerRequest the final meter reading
Within two business daysVillageConfirms the request and reports any open permit or inspection items
Three business days before closingVillagePerforms the final read
Before stamps issueSellerPays the final utility bill and other village balances such as parking tickets
Before closingBuyerSubmits the declaration form, pays the tax and prints the digital stamps

Two copies of the declaration go to the closing, and one copy with the stamps attached is filed with the Cook County Recorder of Deeds. A buyer claiming an exempt transfer under Chapter 9-15.6 of the village code must supply the same supporting documents filed with the Recorder.

sections.h2: What are Wilmette's utility rates for the final bill?
sections.html:
Wilmette bills water, sewer and refuse quarterly, so the final bill can include a partial quarter. The village lists these charges:

  • Water at $2.75 per 100 cubic feet.
  • Sewer at $4.40 per 100 cubic feet.
  • Refuse collection at $28.65 per month.
  • A quarterly meter fee set by meter size, from $0.67 for a 5/8 inch meter to $63.33 for a 4 inch meter.
  • A stormwater utility fee that varies by property.

The village is also switching out nearly 9,000 automated meter reading devices, and the meter replacement program covers meters 15 years of age and older. Ask Finance whether your property's meter is on the replacement list before the final read.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Wilmette homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied median value at $810,600 for 2020 to 2024, and owners live in 87.9% of homes. Median gross rent is $1,978 and median household income is $190,662.

  • The July 2025 estimate is 27,459 residents, 2.5% below the 2020 base of 28,172.
  • Households number 10,287 and average 2.66 people.
  • About 83.6% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.
  • Owner costs with a mortgage are reported as $4,000 or more a month, the top of the Census scale.
  • Mean travel time to work is 34.6 minutes.

At that price level the village's report of open permit and inspection items matters, because an unresolved permit tends to surface just when a buyer is waiting on the stamps.

sections.h2: How are Wilmette property taxes assessed?
sections.html:
Wilmette sits in New Trier Township in Cook County. The township, which also covers Glencoe, Winnetka, Kenilworth and parts of Glenview and Northfield, was reassessed in 2025. New values came out April 23, 2025, total assessed value grew 39%, and appeals were due June 5, 2025. The Assessor's release put the 2024 median single-family sale price at $1,314,000 and the Assessor's median market value estimate for that class at $1,186,000.

Cook County said second-installment bills reflecting the reassessment would be issued September 1, 2026, with an October 1 due date, and it reassesses one-third of the county every year. Request your latest bill from the Cook County Treasurer before listing, and expect the title company to prorate the tax at closing.

sections.h2: What programs and plans affect Wilmette homeowners?
sections.html:
The village runs a Green Homes Incentive Program that makes one-time payments to owners for eligible sustainable home installations. Its Comprehensive Plan also calls for a Historic Preservation Plan, a tool for preserving and rehabilitating historic homes and structures, with a project website.

Wilmette plans a $44.84 million capital program for 2026, focused on roads and water systems. For a seller, street or water main work may be under way near a listing. Building permit questions go to the Community Development Department at 847-853-7550.

sections.h2: What should Wilmette landlords know before selling a rental?
sections.html:
A rental sale follows the same stamp and final read rules, but the village adds a few account details. Landlords are asked to tell Finance when a property is leased, so the village can inform both landlord and tenant about account issues. For a tenant moving out, the final meter read is done on the first available business day closest to the move-out date, and rental service requests are submitted online with the property address and request type.

If you are selling with a tenant in the home, coordinate the move-out date and the closing date with Finance, because the owner's final read for a sale is a separate request from a tenant's. New homeowners should also contact Finance to set up the water account in the right name.

The village grew up along the railroad. Tracks of the Chicago and Milwaukee line were laid in 1855, a station opened in 1869 and the second station, finished by 1874, still stands. Central School, the first public school, opened in a one-room schoolhouse in 1871. Much of what is now west Wilmette was once the separate village of Gross Point, settled by German-speaking Catholic farmers from the Mosel Valley and incorporated in 1874. Knowing that history helps explain why housing in the village ranges from lakefront blocks to farm-era lots farther west.

Wilmette lies on Lake Michigan about 14 miles north of the Loop, bordering Kenilworth, Winnetka, Skokie, Northfield, Glenview and Evanston. It is named for Archange and Antoine Ouilmette, whose 1,280 acre reservation was granted in 1829, and it incorporated as a village on September 19, 1872. The Bahá'í House of Worship, the only one in North America, stands here. The village has held Tree City status since 1983, and its parkways hosted more than 18,600 trees as of 2006.

Public elementary schools belong to Wilmette Public Schools District 39, with Marie Murphy School in Avoca District 37, and high school students attend New Trier High School. The CTA Purple Line ends at Linden Avenue, and Metra's Union Pacific North service stops at Green Bay Road.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wilmette transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer. The village charges $3 for every $1,000 of consideration, or fraction of $1,000, and the buyer buys the stamps. The seller's part is to pay the final utility bill so the stamps can be released.

faqs.q: How early do I request a final meter reading in Wilmette?
faqs.a: Request it about two weeks before the date it is needed. Finance confirms within two business days, and the read takes place three business days before closing.

faqs.q: Where do the Wilmette transfer stamps go?
faqs.a: Two copies of the declaration go to the closing. One copy, with the stamps affixed, is filed with the Cook County Recorder of Deeds. The village can issue the stamps digitally for printing.
Yes. New Trier Township, which includes Wilmette, was reassessed in 2025, and appeals closed June 5, 2025. Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Wilmette?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $810,600 for owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024. Median household income is $190,662 and 87.9% of homes are owner-occupied.
